request: Analyze GSE194193 for PMID 35198907 (Intravenous nicotinamide riboside elevates mouse skeletal muscle NAD(+) without impacting respiratory capacity or insulin sensitivity.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk mRNA-seq (TruSeq stranded, NovaSeq 52-bp PE), quadriceps muscle, male C57BL/6NTac mice on western diet
final.sample_inclusion: 2^3 full factorial, 8 groups x 8 mice = 64; 2 mice removed (stroke at surgery; button infection) -> 62 (S4.3.2.p1, S4.4.1.p1)
final.primary_estimand: Main effect of 4 weeks of voluntary wheel running (VWR vs sedentary) on quadriceps gene expression, averaged over the NR and PT arms; wheels locked before the last dark phase, so a chronic training effect, not acute exercise
planned_contrasts: VWR main effect (S2.6.p3; paper: 2,245 protein-coding genes at q < 0.05)
NR main effect (S2.6.p1; paper: 4 protein-coding genes: Nmrk2 down, Art3, Myh8, Mymk up)
NR x PT x VWR interactions (S2.6.p1; paper: none at q < 0.05)
final.paper_method: edgeR v3.30.3 quasi-likelihood NB GLM, ~ group + RIN, group = 4 (or 8) combinations of NR, VWR (and PT); effects from contrasts between group levels; FDR q-values (S4.4.10.p3)

paper_results.VWR: 2,245 protein-coding genes q < 0.05; Art3 down (q=0.019), Mymk down (q=0.006); Cd38, Sirt3, Sirt5 up; NAD+ synthesis genes (Nmrk1, Nmrk2, Nmnat1, Nmnat3, Nadsyn1, Naprt, Qprt, Nampt) unchanged
paper_results.NR: Nmrk2 down about 65%, Art3 up, Myh8 up, Mymk up
paper_results.GO: camera GO, top-10 terms up with VWR (Fig 6J)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S4.3.2.p1 describes the 2x2x2 factorial with VWR as the exercise factor; S4.4.10.p3 gives the edgeR QL model ~ group + RIN with group-level contrasts; S2.6.p1/p3 give q < 0.05 counts restricted to protein-coding genes. The methods say 4 (or 8) groups without saying which model produced the VWR count; the main figures pool PT (PT had no effect), so both variants are run.

checks: key resources table lists GEO: GSE194193 as RNA-seq data from this paper
metadata: quadriceps, Mus musculus, male, NovaSeq 6000, 62 samples = 64 minus the 2 removed mice
titles encode Training/NR/PT exactly as the 2x2x2 design
data_processing matches STAR 2.7.3a + featureCounts 2.0.0 on GENCODE vM22 (S4.4.10.p3)

ownership.reasoning: Key resources table (RNA-seq data, GEO: GSE194193) and the data availability statement name this series; sample count and factors match S4.3.2.p1.

alignment.reasoning: inspect: metadata title equals the 62 matrix sample columns exactly (62/62). Factor columns come from the GEO characteristics; grp is the 8-cell combination and grp4 the NR x VWR combination used by the paper's ~ group + RIN model. The annotation columns (seqnames, start, end, strand, length) are not samples.

matrix.reasoning: integer fraction 1.0, max 1.85e6, median 0; data_processing says featureCounts output and the supplementary csv holds raw counts; the paper's input is featureCounts counts into edgeR (S4.4.10.p3).

contrasts.expr: mean of the 4 VWR cells - mean of the 4 SED cells

contrasts.expr: mean of the 4 NR cells - mean of the 4 saline cells

contrasts.name: pt_main_PT_vs_noPT
contrasts.expr: mean of the 4 PT cells - mean of the 4 noPT cells

contrasts.name: VWR simple effects within each NR x PT cell

design.reasoning: S4.3.2.p1: balanced 2^3 factorial; S4.4.10.p3: one group-means model over all cells, effects found by comparing the levels encoded by group. S2.6.p1 reports main effects because no interaction reached q < 0.05. The exercise estimand is the VWR main effect averaged over NR and PT; the four planned simple effects are its components. Every cell has 7-8 mice.

candidates.value: two-group VWR vs SED pooling all other arms (~ train)
candidates.reason_rejected: drops the NR/PT cells that the paper's group model keeps

candidates.value: 4-group model (NR x VWR, PT pooled) as primary
candidates.reason_rejected: the paper's 4 (or 8) wording allows it; run as sensitivity because the 8-group model uses the full design

covariates.name: rin
covariates.disposition: included as a continuous covariate, as in the paper's ~ group + RIN (S4.4.10.p3)

covariates.name: cohort
covariates.disposition: not included: the paper does not model it; balanced across VWR (15/16 per cohort); checked in the confounding report only

covariates.name: purification_pool, day_of_termination, time_of_termination
covariates.disposition: not included: not in the paper's model

covariance.reasoning: One sample per independent mouse, no repeated measures. The paper adjusts for RIN only; other recorded processing columns are not added because of their names.

deviations: low-expression filter not stated in the paper; filterByExpr applied as the edgeR manual recommends (assumption)
main effect computed as the mean of the 4 VWR cells minus the mean of the 4 SED cells; the paper does not state its contrast weights

method.reasoning: Raw featureCounts counts support the paper's edgeR QL route directly; tools.r_de_tools:run_r_de with engine edger_ql runs R edgeR on an arbitrary design with makeContrasts expressions, so the main-effect contrast over the cell-means model is expressible.

final.deviation_note: the paper counts only protein-coding genes; our tables include all GENCODE genes passing filterByExpr, so a protein-coding subset count is reported separately in HANDBACK.md

threshold.reasoning: S2.6.p1 and S2.6.p3: q-value cutoff 0.05 (FDR), no fold-change rule.

caveats: the paper's VWR count (2,245) is protein-coding genes only; our total count includes non-coding genes
the paper does not say whether the VWR count came from the 4- or 8-group model; both are run

study.reasoning: The route reproduces the paper's edgeR QL ~ group + RIN model with FDR < 0.05.

discrepancies.item: gene universe of the reported count
discrepancies.data: matrix holds 55,487 GENCODE vM22 genes of all biotypes without a biotype column

discrepancies.item: number of groups in the model
